name: Helcim for WooCommerce
author: Helcim

sections.description:
Helcim for WooCommerce lets you accept all major credit cards and GooglePay directly on your WordPress store while saving on processing fees. This free plugin connects your store to your Helcim account and processes payments through HelcimPay.js — a secure, hosted checkout that handles card data for you, reducing your PCI compliance scope.

Order management stays within WooCommerce but payments run on Helcim’s transparent interchange-plus pricing: you pay the true cost from the card networks plus one clear margin, with no monthly fee, no PCI fee, and rates that fall automatically as your volume grows.

REQUIREMENTS:
– A Helcim account (free to create)
– Generated Helcim API token
– WordPress and WooCommerce installed and active
– A valid SSL certificate (HTTPS) on your store
– Supported versions:
– WordPress: 6.6+
– PHP: 7.4+
– WooCommerce: 10.5+
– A business based in the United States or Canada, processing in USD or CAD
sections.installation:
Step 1: Create a Helcim account – Sign up for free in minutes — no paperwork, no commitments, no monthly fee. Start here.

Step 2: Generate an API token – Once your account is approved, generate your API token. You can do this by Integrations > API Configuration > Create an API token. This token will securely link your Helcim account to your WooCommerce store later.

Step 3: Install the Helcim for WooCommerce (v5) plugin

You can install the plugin directly from your WordPress admin dashboard or download it manually from the WordPress Plugin Directory or WooCommerce Marketplace.

Install from the WordPress Admin Dashboard

  1. Log in to your WordPress admin dashboard.
  2. Navigate to Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  3. Search for Helcim for WooCommerce.
  4. Select the Helcim plugin from the search results to view its details.
  5. Click Install Now, then Activate once the installation is complete.

Once the plugin is activated, you can proceed with connecting it to your Helcim account using the API token generated in Step 2.

Step 4: Configure your checkout – In WordPress, go to Payments › Helcim and hit Manage. Set up how you want to get paid:
– Title: The payment method name your customer sees at checkout.
– Description: The payment method description shown to customers at checkout.
– Environment: Choose where to deploy the plugin — Sandbox (testing) or Live.
– Live API token: The token you created, linking WooCommerce to Helcim.
– Branding and others: Add your logo and brand colors, enable Google Pay, and let customers securely save their card for future purchases

Step 5: Test a live transaction. Run a real payment end-to-end to make sure everything’s wired up correctly before you go live. Your first $5 in card transactions is fee-free — test it through and through, on us.
sections.faq:
Can Helcim reduce WooCommerce transaction fees?

Yes. Processing your WooCommerce payments through Helcim uses transparent interchange-plus pricing, which is often lower than typical flat-rate WooCommerce payment options — and the margin drops automatically as your monthly volume grows.

Does the integration require an API?

Yes. The plugin uses a Helcim API token to process payments and sync refunds and tokenized customer payment details through Helcim’s payment system. Order management stays in WooCommerce.

How do I access the integration?

Install the Helcim for WooCommerce plugin in WordPress, then connect your Helcim API credentials in your WooCommerce payment settings.

Is there a cost to use the integration?

No. The plugin is free, and you only pay standard Helcim processing fees on the transactions you run.

Does it support recurring payments or subscriptions?

Not in this release. WooCommerce Subscriptions and automated recurring billing are planned for a future version.

Which currencies are supported?

Both CAD and USD are supported.
sections.changelog:
5.0.2

  • Fixed credit card payments failing with a generic “Could not complete transaction” message on some carts — most often with tax-inclusive pricing, quantities greater than one, or coupons — caused by a rounding mismatch in the invoice line items.
  • Fixed an issue where retrying the same cart after a declined or cancelled payment could fail.
  • Fixed the payment window occasionally failing to open, or checkout getting stuck with no message, when the payment provider was slow to respond — a clear “please try again” notice now appears instead.
  • Fixed successful payments not being recorded on the order — leaving it stuck in “Pending payment” and later cancelled — on stores not installed at the main website address, such as sites in a subfolder, multisite networks, or multilingual sites.
  • Helcim invoices now describe the tax by rate with each amount, such as “Sales Tax: $6.14, State Tax: $3.07”, rather than showing only a total.
  • Helcim invoices now note the discount total and the coupon codes used when an order has a coupon applied.
  • Checkout failures that happen in the shopper’s browser — such as the payment window not opening — are now recorded in the WooCommerce log for easier troubleshooting.
  • Debug logging now masks identifying customer details, so logs can be shared with support more safely.
  • Tested up to WooCommerce 10.9

5.0.1

  • Fixed invoice number generation for orders.
  • Fixed entryPoint parameter in payment request.
  • Tested up to WordPress 6.9.5
  • Tested up to WooCommerce 9.9.3

5.0.0

  • New platform release built on the HelcimPay.js checkout modal.
  • Sandbox and live environments with separate API tokens and an in-settings API connection test.
  • Branding & appearance controls (logo, brand color, light/dark/system theme, corner radius, payment button text).
  • Optional Google Pay and Apple Pay in the modal.
  • Support for the WooCommerce Cart/Checkout blocks and High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Automatic migration of v4 settings on upgrade.
